crash_hull.source: Points that hit the ground first (le frame): wing tips (60 in span, slight dihedral), spinner tip (firewall 6.94 in ahead of LE plus engine and spinner), tail end and stabilizer tips (52 in overall length), fin top, belly under the CG (fuselage bottom 0.053 m below the thrust line, from the model team's fuselage stations). Read from the Jensen plan and the visual model. Since E1 the wheels are landing_gear contacts, not hull points: a wheel on the ground is a landing, a leg pushed past its travel is a crash

landing_gear.description: E1: the wheels as spring-damper contacts with the flat ground (physics/ground_contact.gd): F_up = max(0, k·compression + c·rate) at each wheel bottom. Stiffness from the ROADMAP E1 rule ω·dt < 0.1 (ω = sqrt(Σk/m) at the 240 Hz tick), checked by the loader; the CG must lie inside the wheel footprint. E2: tyre forces in the ground plane along each wheel's heading: rolling resistance C_rr·N and a slip-angle side force saturating at μ·N (friction circle); the nose wheel steers with the rudder servo. Coefficients are for a tyre on dry pavement; per-surface factors (grass) come with the field surfaces (E3). Brakes: none.

position.source: GP-06b: wheel bottoms from research/ugly-stik/model-v3/equipment-handoff.json nominal_ground_contact_le_m (model-v3 axle at model y -0.22 m is 0.215 m below the thrust line, shaft_y -0.005 m; minus the wheel radius 0.0381 m), so physics and the rendered wheels touch the same ground. E1 read the axle as 0.22 m below the thrust line: every Stik contact sat 5 mm below its drawn wheel and the rendered wheels floated 5 mm. x: mains 0.094 m aft of the plan CG (D9d hull, model-v3 axle x_aft 0.215 m), nose 0.257 m ahead; track 0.36 m. Tricycle: the CG sits 27 % of the wheelbase from the mains, so the airplane stands on its nose wheel

max_steering.source: Nose wheel steering at full rudder, linked to the rudder servo. RC tricycle setups use about 15-25° (less throw than the rudder's, to avoid swerving at speed); 20° gives a kinematic turn radius of wheelbase/tan 20° = 0.351/0.364 = 0.96 m at walking speed. Guess, not measured; JSBSim's full-size C172 uses 10°

rolling_resistance.source: Rolling resistance coefficient on dry pavement. Borrowed base 0.022 (JSBSim c172x rolling_friction, a full-size tyre on concrete), doubled for a 76 mm RC wheel (resistance grows as the wheel shrinks: deformation and bumps are larger relative to the radius). Guess; a coast-down on the owner's field would measure it (E2 report)

side_friction.source: Peak tyre friction coefficient μ on dry pavement: JSBSim c172x static_friction 0.8 (github.com/JSBSim-Team/jsbsim, aircraft/c172x/c172x.xml). One value for side force and friction circle (JSBSim's 0.5 dynamic friction for a skid is not modelled). Grass is lower (E3, field surfaces)

peak_slip_angle.source: Slip angle where the side force reaches μ·N in our linear-then-saturated law. Matches the initial slope of JSBSim's default Pacejka side-force curve (FGLGear: stiffness 0.06/deg, shape 2.8, curvature 1.03; slope at zero μ·2.8·0.06 per degree, so μ is reached linearly at 1/0.168 = 5.95°). A small RC wheel's real curve is unmeasured. Also sets the low-speed damping the loader checks: μ·g·dt/(tan 6°·1 m/s) = 0.31 at 240 Hz

breakaway_factor.source: E3b1: static ÷ rolling resistance of a wheel at rest (bearing and axle friction, tyre flat spot, the small mound in front of a wheel parked on grass). The ground knowledge base (docs/research/roadmap-investigations/04, §3) brackets it at 1.0-1.5 without a measurement; 1.25 is the middle. On the mown runway the hold is 1.25 × 2.8 N = 3.5 N against 2.6 N of idle thrust; on dry pavement 1.4 N, so the Stik rolls at idle there. A luggage-scale pull on the owner's field (breakaway force, then the steady rolling force) would measure it

aero.source: OpenFlightSim UltraStick25e AeroOpenFlight.xml @ b020511 (sha256 43ff5c1e…); nondimensional, applied to the Ugly Stik as a geometrically similar Stik; Cmq, CLq and Cnr derived from the Stik itself (D11g)

CL_max.source: Whole-airplane maximum lift: mid value of the CLmax 1.0-1.2 assumed in the ROADMAP predicted-handling table (semi-symmetric Jensen section, Re about 3e5); gives a 1-g stall near 9.0 m/s

CL_min.source: Negative stall of a semi-symmetric section is weaker than the positive one; assumed about 0.7 x CL_max

stall_blend_width.source: Width of the smooth transition from attached flow to flat-plate flow (PicaSim uses a cosine ramp of about 10 deg, YASim a stall-width parameter); the start is solved so the lift peak equals CL_max

CD90.source: Flat-plate drag of the finite wing at 90 deg: Viterna CDmax = 1.11 + 0.018 AR with AR = b^2/S = 5.0 (NASA CR-1983, RESEARCH.md plan review #3)

sideslip_blend.source: Sideslip range where the linear beta terms (CYb, Clb, Cnb) give way to their sin(beta) form, finite and restoring up to knife edge

conventions.rates: p_hat = p·b/(2V), q_hat = q·c/(2V), r_hat = r·b/(2V)
conventions.elevator: per radian, positive = trailing edge DOWN (dCm/dElev < 0)
conventions.aileron: per radian per surface, positive = trailing edge DOWN; right and left listed separately
conventions.rudder: per radian, positive = trailing edge LEFT (dCn/dRud < 0)
conventions.axes: lift, drag, side force in wind axes; roll, pitch, yaw moments in body axes about the aero reference point

CLq.source: research/aero/d11g/derive_rate_derivatives.gd (D11g/R02, ARP-referred since D6e-R1): current section-plane-source-weighted-wake-velocity-v2 local-law central difference at the 15 m/s level trim, controls neutral and dimensional wake settled. About-CG CLq=2.0034. Model-derived, not measured or physically validated.

CYdr.source: docs/research/flight-repair-implementation.md: provisional surface model; estimated, not measured flight data; CYdr=a_v*S_v/S*tau; Cndr=-CYdr*l/b; Cldr=CYdr*(z_v-z_ARP)/b; Cnb=a_v*S_v/S*l/b

body_cn_beta.source: D10-R2 (docs/research/flight-dynamics/stik-lateral-directional-2026-10-18, research/flight-dynamics/stik-lateral-directional/directional_prediction.py): (0.684 - 1) x fin term 0.12741 for the DATCOM high-wing fin efficiency eta_v(1 + dsigma/dbeta), plus Raymer eq. 16.50 fuselage term -0.0130 from the plan stations; placed in the body couple as the P-51 does; not measured

downwash_gradient.source: E0a2: dε/dα at the horizontal tail point from a flat-wing vortex lattice of the AR 5 rectangular wing (docs/research/roadmap-investigations/02-aerodynamics-rc-scale.md T2: VLM 0.457; elliptic estimate 2·CLα/(πA) = 0.50). Generic rectangular-wing fit, not measured on this airplane; docs/research/ground-effect/M5-GE-1/README.md

downwash_coefficient.source: fit of the T6 image-VLM tail downwash ratios per unit wing lift (same-alpha ratios 0.27/0.49/0.67/0.90/0.98 divided by the same-alpha lift ratios 1.35/1.16/1.09/1.03/1.01 at wing h/b 0.10/0.17/0.25/0.5/1.0) by 25(h/b)^2 / (1 + 25(h/b)^2), within 0.03 up to h/b 0.5; estimated for the AR 5 wing with the tail 0.05 m below it; docs/research/ground-effect/M5-GE-1/README.md

downwash_exponent.source: fit of the T6 image-VLM tail downwash ratios per unit wing lift (same-alpha ratios 0.27/0.49/0.67/0.90/0.98 divided by the same-alpha lift ratios 1.35/1.16/1.09/1.03/1.01 at wing h/b 0.10/0.17/0.25/0.5/1.0) by 25(h/b)^2 / (1 + 25(h/b)^2), within 0.03 up to h/b 0.5; estimated for the AR 5 wing with the tail 0.05 m below it; docs/research/ground-effect/M5-GE-1/README.md

propulsion.description: D5 thrust v0: engine rpm follows throttle with a first-order lag; thrust and torque from propeller coefficients at the current advance ratio. In-flight prop unloading (rpm rising with airspeed) waits for the shaft model (G2).

max_rpm_static.source: power balance: engine power assumed linear in rpm below the peak (estimated) = static prop power Cp·ρ·n³·D⁵ with Cp 0.0471 → n = sqrt(P_peak/n_peak / (Cp·ρ·D⁵))

idle_rpm.source: NITRO-02 experimental installation estimate; no matched hardware measurement
